memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "Make the robe of the ephod entirely of blue cloth, with an opening for the head in its center. There shall be a woven edge like a collar around this opening, so that it will not tear." - Exodus 28:31-32 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The robe had a reinforced collar around the head opening, woven specifically "so that it will not tear." The point of greatest strain — where the garment was pulled over the head repeatedly — was strengthened in advance. God anticipated the wear and built in the reinforcement before it was needed.

That is a picture of wisdom. The places most likely to tear are known in advance, and they can be strengthened before the strain comes. We often wait until something has already ripped before attending to it. God's design works the other way: reinforce first, at the point where pressure is predictable.

You probably know where your own strain points are — the situation that always tests your patience, the season that always leaves you depleted, the relationship where you consistently fray. Rather than waiting for the tear, strengthen it now. Jesus told His disciples to watch and pray so they would not fall into temptation, knowing the spirit is willing but the flesh is weak (Matt 26:41). Where do you predictably come under pressure? Reinforce that edge today, before the pulling starts.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Where are the predictable "strain points" in my life that need reinforcing?
What could I put in place now, before pressure comes, rather than after?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You strengthen things before they tear. Show me my weak points and help me reinforce them now through prayer and wisdom, before the strain comes. Amen.
